Beginner: A fruit seller records the temperature before opening and the mangoes sold by closing. Which value can be a morning input?
Temperature is available before opening.
temperature
A handwritten digit is paired with its verified digit 7. What is the label?
The label is the verified answer, 7.
7/seven
What is learned when a program adjusts its lunch-per-person ratio from past sales?
A model setting, the ratio, is learned from observed examples.
setting/ratio
example/data
Intermediate: A coach forecasts half as many water bottles as runners. For 26 runners, what forecast does this rule give?
Half of 26 is 13 bottles.
13/thirteen
An ice seller must decide at noon. The spreadsheet has morning temperature and the final daily bill. Which clue can be used honestly?
Use morning temperature because the final daily bill becomes known later.
temperature
later/after
A rule always forecasts 12 tickets. Sales are 10, 13 and 16. What is its average absolute miss?
The errors have sizes 2, 1 and 4. The average is 7/3 tickets, about 2.33.
A training set has only holiday customers. The owner wants weekday predictions. Which new examples would help?
Collect weekday customers with their actual purchases.
weekday
purchase/sale
A machine predicts 80 arrivals. Counting later reveals 74. Which number should become the observed outcome for this day?
Store 74 as the label, preserving 80 separately as the forecast.
label/outcome
Advanced: Every busy-day item sells out by noon. How could a model trained on sales alone underestimate demand?
Sales stop at the stock limit. Record stockouts or unserved requests to detect unmet demand.
stock/sell
unserved/unmet
A predictor beats last week's guess on 3 days and loses on 7. Can the number of wins alone settle the comparison?
Compare the size or cost of every miss. Three large gains may outweigh seven small losses.
size/magnitude/cost
large/outweigh
A booking assistant knows a customer's refund reason only after cancellation. How would you detect accidental use of it in pre-booking forecasts?
Replay a historical request from a timestamped snapshot of fields available at booking. Exclude the later refund reason.
snapshot/timestamp/available
refund/later
A class selector recommends popular workshops. Attendance rises after recommendations start. What makes it hard to judge whether the model discovered existing interest?
The recommendation itself can change attendance. Compare with a suitable control group to measure its effect.
recommendation
control/comparison
Delivery forecasts worsen after a bridge closes, although the code and model version stay fixed. What evidence would distinguish changed conditions from a software bug?
Compare errors by route and date around the closure and replay saved inputs on the same version.
route/date
replay/version

Beginner: Which asset tells a supervised spam filter whether an old message was spam?
A verified spam or ordinary label attached to the message.
label
A customer grouping program receives purchases without category names. What type of learning fits that setup?
Unsupervised learning can discover groups without supplied answers.
unsupervised
What does a cluster number such as 4 tell you about the quality of its members?
By itself it is only an identifier. It gives no quality ranking.
identifier/name
ranking/rank
Intermediate: A service has complaints with a known handling department and wants to route new complaints. What training approach fits?
Use supervised learning with the recorded department as the label.
supervised
department
A gardener has photographs with no species names and wants to discover visually similar batches. Which approach can start immediately?
Cluster the photos using visual similarity, then inspect samples from each group.
cluster
similar/inspect
Family size is measured from 1 to 6 and household spending from 0 to 50000. Why might raw distance cluster households mainly by spending?
Differences in spending have a much larger numerical scale and can dominate the distance.
spending
scale/dominat
A music app groups listeners by how often they listen, but wants groups based on preferred genre. What input change matters?
Use genre preferences or listening shares by genre instead of only total play count.
genre
share/preference
A batch of 12 mystery objects gets clustered into groups of 7 and 5. How many verified category labels has the clustering operation supplied?
Zero verified labels. Group membership alone does not establish what each object actually is.
zero/0
verified/category
Advanced: Two experts disagree on which complaint department is correct. What work should precede a supervised routing benchmark?
Agree on labeling rules and review disputed examples before judging predictions against those answers.
rule/guideline
disput/review
A clustering algorithm returns eight tidy groups, but a librarian says each mixes unrelated subjects. How would you evaluate usefulness?
Inspect examples with the librarian against the intended shelving purpose and adjust the similarity measure if needed.
librarian/inspect
similarity/purpose
A shop wants to infer a customer's true age from a purchase cluster. Why is naming a cluster 'young' insufficient evidence?
Purchasing similarity need not identify age. Verify against independently obtained age labels before claiming that relationship.
similarity/purchase
label/verify
Two groupings differ only in their assigned numbers. How can a fair stability comparison avoid declaring every item changed?
Compare which pairs of items stay together or match groups by shared members before comparing labels.
pair/member
together/shared
A factory has millions of unlabelled sounds and only 50 engineer-confirmed faults. How could both resources guide inspection without pretending every unusual sound is defective?
Use unlabelled sounds to find unusual patterns, then validate flagged sounds with engineer-confirmed faults and new inspections.
unusual/pattern
validate/inspection

Beginner: A shop estimates parcel weight in kilograms. Is the prediction a category or a numerical amount?
It is a numerical amount measured in kilograms.
amount/numeric
kilogram/kg
A fare rule adds 8 rupees for every additional kilometre. What does the 8 represent?
It is the slope, or price change per kilometre.
slope/change
kilometre/km
A repair actually takes 47 minutes after a prediction of 40. What is actual minus predicted?
The residual is positive 7 minutes.
7/seven
Intermediate: A printer quotes 15 rupees setup plus 3 per page. Estimate the cost of 8 pages.
15 + 3 × 8 gives 39 rupees.
Fare receipts show 70 rupees at 3 km and 90 at 5 km. Assuming a straight-line pattern, what is the starting charge?
The rate is 10 per km. Subtract 30 from 70 to get a starting charge of 40 rupees.
10/ten
40/forty
A route predictor misses by 4 minutes too high and 8 minutes too low. Calculate the mean absolute error.
The absolute misses are 4 and 8, giving a mean of 6 minutes.
6/six
Predicted bills are 80 and 90 while actual bills are 75 and 85. Which direction is the bias on these two bills?
Both predictions are high by 5. Actual minus predicted is negative on both.
high/over
5/five
A house-price line assigns a 30-square-metre room a negative price. Before showing it, what should the app inspect?
Check whether such small homes were in the training range and whether the line is appropriate there.
range/training
line/model
Advanced: A flat delivery fee plus a per-kilometre charge changes to a higher rate after 10 km. Why might one straight line miss both short and long trips?
One straight line assumes a constant slope. Compare a rule with separate slopes on either side of 10 km using held-back trips.
slope/rate
separate/held
Two fare models have the same average absolute miss, but one severely underquotes trips with tolls. What comparison would expose it?
Separate toll trips and inspect signed residuals or underquote costs on that group.

Squaring magnifies the large miss. Verify the original transaction before changing or excluding that record.
squar
verify/original
A customer asks for an exact arrival promise based on a regression estimate of 22 minutes. What historical evidence would support a range instead?
Measure held-back errors for similar trips and report how often a proposed interval actually contained the arrival.
held/similar
interval/contained
A bakery wants the number of cakes to prepare, while a fitted line produces 4.6. How should rounding be chosen?
Compare the costs of overstock and shortage on real outcomes; choose the rounding policy that reflects those costs.
cost
shortage/overstock

Beginner: An email filter chooses spam or ordinary. What is a class in this example?
Spam and ordinary are the two possible outcome categories.
spam
ordinary

Yes. Equality is included in the cutoff.
yes
equality/included

It is a false negative because a real damaged case was missed.
false negative

Two scores qualify, 0.5 and 0.8.
two/2
A queue flags 12 parcels. Nine have damage. How many flags were false alarms?
Three flags were false alarms, from 12 minus 9.
3/three
A road detector found 6 real potholes and missed 2. What fraction of real potholes did it find?
It found 6 of 8, or 75 percent.

It changes from spam to ordinary because 0.68 falls below the new threshold.
spam
ordinary

Allow multiple labels for one parcel, including both fragile and perishable.
multiple/both
label

Evaluate how many verified frauds occur in the top 20 and how many real frauds stay outside that budget.
20/twenty
outside/miss
An alarm catches most faults in one factory but generates many false alarms at a second. Which score breakdown could explain the difference?
Inspect score distributions by true condition and factory, together with the fault prevalence at each site.
factory/site

Group many cases with scores near 0.7 and compare their actual positive rate with 70 percent.

positive
denominator/fraction

Estimate missed-case and false-alarm costs on held-back labeled cases, then compare total cost at candidate thresholds.
cost
threshold/candidate

Beginner: Which portion of a home-price dataset teaches the model its settings?
The training portion supplies the examples used for learning.
training
What should happen to final test answers while you choose features?
Keep the final test answers held back from feature selection.
held/hidden
feature

Data leakage lets a future value enter an earlier prediction.
leakage
future

Days 25 through 30 form the test.

Keep every picture of the same cat in one partition.
cat
partition/together

Recall for broken devices cannot be measured because there are zero actual positives in the test sample.
recall
zero/no

Use 12, the value learned from the training homes.
training

It became a validation set used for selection. A fresh test set is needed for a final estimate.
validation
fresh/new
Advanced: A customer app predicts later purchases for existing shoppers and also serves entirely new shoppers. Why report two split designs?
A chronological test measures future use for existing shoppers; a customer-held-out test measures transfer to unseen shoppers.
chronological/time
customer/unseen
A duplicate sale appears with slightly different spelling in train and test. What audit catches leakage beyond exact text matches?
Match by stable sale ID or other event identity and inspect near duplicates across partitions.
id/identit
duplicate/partition

A training label window can reach into test dates. Leave a gap or exclude crossing windows before evaluation.
window
gap/exclude

event
held/new

Treat it as development evidence, record the decisions made from it and reserve a later untouched period for confirmation.
development
untouched/later

Beginner: If a delivery lasted from 9:10 to 9:25, what feature expresses its duration in minutes?
The elapsed time is 15 minutes.
15/fifteen
A route is named Blue. Does the name give a natural numerical ordering?
No. It is a category without a natural numerical order.
category
order
What does an on-or-off feature for Sunday record?
It records whether the date is Sunday, often as 1 for yes and 0 for no.
sunday
yes/1

180 divided by 3 gives 60 rupees per visit.
60/sixty
A scooter leaves at 23:55 and returns at 00:10 the next day. What must be kept to derive a 15-minute duration?
Keep the dates and clock times so midnight is handled correctly.
date
midnight
A route-name feature is built from training labels Red and Blue. An unseen Green route arrives. What policy is needed?
Use a documented unknown-category representation or a clear rejection rule.
unknown/reject
A café predicts before opening. Available fields are yesterday’s cups sold, today’s forecast and today’s closing receipts. Which field must be excluded?
Exclude today’s closing receipts because they occur after the morning decision.
closing
after
A room count is missing in one listing while another has zero rooms listed by mistake. Why store a separate missing flag?
The flag distinguishes an unknown count from a recorded zero, enabling a later quality check.
unknown
zero

The endpoints represent adjacent times. A cyclic encoding can preserve their closeness across midnight.
adjacent/close
cyclic/circular
A merchant target-encodes a product by its average refund rate, including the order being scored. What leakage-safe computation could replace it?

out-of-fold/past
mapping/training

Measure live coverage and errors with the intended missing-value fallback on realistic cases.
coverage

isolat/contribution
example/condition

Precision measures that share.
precision

Error analysis can reveal a recurring kind of mistake hidden by an overall average.

False negatives, because actual failures were predicted healthy.

6 divided by 10 gives 60 percent precision.

Recall is 8 divided by 10, or 80 percent.
A forecast has actual waits 5 and 9 and predicts 7 and 6. What is its average absolute miss?
The absolute errors are 2 and 3, averaging 2.5 minutes.
A stock model matches 92 of 100 labels. The most common label alone occurs 94 times. Does accuracy show improvement over the majority baseline?
No. The baseline scores 94 percent and the model scores 92 percent.
A restaurant has one severe late delivery among nine on-time deliveries. Which extra measurement would show how bad the delay was?
Report the delay duration or minutes late for the severe case alongside the count.

Uninspected mail lacks verified outcomes, so missed positives outside the inspected sample are unknown.
uninspected

Evaluate more representative independent customers and quantify uncertainty in the paired difference.
representative/independent
uncertainty

Group sizes weight the average. Inspect scores and counts by region and use weights matching the intended population.
weight

separate

It fits the training examples but fails to generalize to new cases.
training

What do we call a held-back set used during model selection?
A validation set.
validation
If a model can fit many highly detailed patterns, what property is large?
Its capacity is large.
capacity

Overfitting is increasing as the rule fits training detail that hurts validation performance.
overfit

Limit tree depth or require more examples per leaf.

unit
